Snow patches and dark exposed ground across the Cairngorm mountains, with an RAF rescue helicopter in the foreground.
Winter in the Cairngorms during a rescue-training flight. Bright snow reflects more sunlight than the darker exposed ground; patchy cover changes the landscape's albedo.
Snow-covered Mount Adams viewed from the Naches Loop Trail in Washington.
Mount Adams, Washington. This Cascade arc volcano is part of the volcanic chain above the Cascadia subduction zone.
Glen Canyon Dam holds back Lake Powell above a narrow river gorge.
Glen Canyon Dam and Lake Powell, Arizona. Reservoir storage and controlled releases alter the timing and size of flows downstream.
Denver's skyline and distant mountain slopes seen from Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge.
Denver, Colorado. The city stands on high plains beside the Rocky Mountains; elevation reduces air pressure compared with sea level.
A car on a Texas Panhandle road beneath a wall of airborne dust during the Dust Bowl.
Texas Panhandle during the Dust Bowl. Wind removed exposed topsoil during severe drought; this photograph records dust in the air, rather than water-cut gullies.
Waves and wet sand beneath Naples Pier on Florida's Gulf coast at sunset.
Naples, Florida. Waves redistribute sediment along a low sandy coast.
Layered cliffs, mesas and deeply incised valleys of the Grand Canyon in evening light.
Grand Canyon from Hopi Point, Arizona. Resistant beds form steps and cliffs above valleys cut by running water.
A physical marker of the historic Greenwich Meridian at the Royal Observatory.
The historic Greenwich Meridian makes a reference longitude tangible. Modern WGS84 zero longitude lies about 102 metres east of this line.
An arching orange lava fountain erupts from a vent on Kīlauea amid dark cooling lava.
Kīlauea, 25 February 1983. USGS photographed a lava fountain approximately 10 metres high; molten rock is at the surface, not throughout the mantle.
Aerial photograph of Spurn Point curving across the Humber estuary entrance.
Spurn Point, England, photographed in 2024. Longshore transport supplies a spit at the Humber estuary.
Slope failures above the coast at Hong Kong's Redhill Peninsula after extreme rainfall.
Redhill Peninsula, Hong Kong. Slope failures following extreme rainfall show how saturated ground can destabilise steep developed slopes.
Steep dark rock walls border the Almannagjá rift at Þingvellir, Iceland.
Almannagjá, Þingvellir: faults accommodate extension within Iceland's broad North American–Eurasian plate boundary zone.
White chalk cliffs, offshore remnants and a wave-cut base near the Pinnacles in Purbeck.
The Pinnacles coast, Purbeck, Dorset. Erosion leaves isolated stacks and lower remnants called stumps beside the retreating chalk cliffs.
Flooded streets and houses in New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina, 2005. Floodwater filled low-lying neighbourhoods after storm surge and flood-protection failures.
Aerial view of abandoned buildings at the Kola Superdeep Borehole site in Russia in 2020.
Kola Superdeep Borehole site, 2020. The deepest borehole reached 12.262 km within continental crust; it did not enter the mantle.
A winding road descends Honister Pass through steep slopes in Cumbria.
Honister Pass, Cumbria. Glacial erosion has shaped the mountain valleys and passes.
Dry, deeply dissected loess slopes near Hunyuan in Shanxi, China.
Loess near Hunyuan, Shanxi. Wind deposited the silt; runoff later cut gullies into the exposed ground.
Visitors and a park ranger stand in the broad limestone Broadway passage of Mammoth Cave, Kentucky.
Broadway passage, Mammoth Cave, Kentucky. Groundwater dissolution enlarged fractures in limestone into a large cave system.
The Mississippi River and Natchez–Vidalia Bridge seen from Natchez, Mississippi.
Natchez, Mississippi. A broad river corridor runs below the bluffs along the state's western boundary.
Aerial view of Bodie Island, its lighthouse, wetlands and Atlantic beach in North Carolina.
Bodie Island, North Carolina. A low barrier island separates Atlantic waves from sheltered wetlands.
Phoenix's skyline, transport surfaces and desert mountains seen from Sky Harbor airport.
Phoenix, Arizona. Built surfaces store heat in a desert city. Air or thermal measurements are needed to quantify the urban heat island; this photograph shows the land cover.
Aerial view of the San Andreas Fault cutting across dry hills in California.
San Andreas Fault in California's Sierra Madre Mountains. The fault accommodates mainly horizontal motion between the Pacific and North American plates.
The Huangpu River curves around Lujiazui's towers in Shanghai.
Shanghai. Dense urban development occupies low delta ground beside the tidal Huangpu River.
Snow on Gallt y Wenallt above mist in Nant Gwynant, Eryri / Snowdonia.
Nant Gwynant, Eryri / Snowdonia. A glacial valley lies beneath the steep Snowdon horseshoe.
Nearly full Moon photographed from Hamois, Belgium, with dark maria and bright cratered highlands.
Nearly full Moon photographed from Hamois, Belgium. The phase is nearly the same for observers in Wales and California at the same instant; local rise times and the disc's orientation differ.
Floodwater surrounds Burrowbridge in the Somerset Levels in February 2014.
Burrowbridge, Somerset, February 2014. Low relief slows the drainage of extensive floodwater.
The Thames Barrier's silver piers beside the tidal river in London.
Thames Barrier, London. Movable gates reduce tidal-surge flood risk upstream; they do not remove every source of river or surface-water flooding.
GOES-East satellite view of the Americas with tropical cloud bands and midlatitude weather systems.

GOES-East observes the Americas from a fixed orbital longitude. Earth's rotation underlies the daily cycle; civil time-zone boundaries are agreed conventions and are not visible in this satellite image.
Satellite view of Typhoon Mangkhut with a compact eye and spiralling cloud bands in September 2018.
Typhoon Mangkhut, September 2018, observed by NASA EOSDIS. The western North Pacific storm later affected the Philippines and southern China; this image is a historical observation.
Meteosat view of Earth's day–night boundary on the December solstice, with more of the Southern Hemisphere in daylight.

Meteosat-9 SEVIRI, 21 December 2010. The tilted day–night boundary gives the Southern Hemisphere longer days. Axial tilt, rather than a change in Earth–Sun distance, controls this seasonal illumination.
Sunlit shingle beach and coastal buildings at Southsea, Portsmouth.
Southsea, Portsmouth. Land and sea warm at different rates in sunshine, creating conditions that can support a sea breeze. A photograph of the coast alone does not measure its wind direction.
Steam and orange microbial mats around Grand Prismatic Spring in Yellowstone National Park.
Grand Prismatic Spring, Yellowstone. Hot groundwater and heat-tolerant microorganisms create the pool's striking colour bands.
People cross pale limestone blocks separated by deep joints above Malham Cove, England.
Malham Cove limestone pavement. Rainwater containing dissolved carbon dioxide widens joints into grykes, leaving blocks called clints.
Yosemite Valley's forested floor between steep granite walls, viewed from Tunnel View.
Yosemite Valley, California. Glacial erosion widened and steepened a pre-existing river valley in granite.
A Puerto Rican soil profile has a dark surface above pale carbonate-rich subsoil, with a depth scale.
Calciustoll near Ponce, Puerto Rico: a Mollisol with a roughly 30 cm mollic surface over a calcic horizon. Its parent material includes colluvium and weathered limestone.
Rounded potholes cut into dark bedrock beside flowing water in the Presque Isle River, Michigan.
Presque Isle River, Michigan. Sediment circulating in eddies abrades the bedrock, enlarging these potholes.
NASA CERES map of reflected shortwave radiation averaged over 2000–2015, with a 0–385 W m⁻² colour scale.

This CERES observation maps reflected sunlight. Solar absorption by the Earth system is the incoming shortwave energy minus this reflected component; the image measures reflection rather than absorption directly.
A hand pump used to draw groundwater at Perambalur, India.
Groundwater hand pump at Perambalur, India. Abstraction removes water from an aquifer; pumping may lower the water level around a well, which is measured below ground.
Polygonal ground and ponds on the tundra in Noatak National Preserve, Alaska, photographed from the air.

Patterned ground in Alaska's Noatak region. The active layer above permafrost thaws and refreezes seasonally; surface patterns show freezing processes, but active-layer depth needs field measurements.
Parallel rows of clouds extend from sea ice across open water in the Bering Sea.
Cloud streets over the Bering Sea, 20 January 2006. Cold air over warmer water supports convection organised into rolls by the wind.
Dense green tropical forest canopy at Bodiman, Cameroon.

Tropical forest at Bodiman, Cameroon. This is a landscape example for tropical rainforest climate; an Af classification is determined from long-term monthly temperature and rainfall, not from vegetation alone.
The Hawaiian volcanic islands stretch across the Pacific beneath scattered white clouds in an ISS photograph.
Hawaii from the ISS. The volcanic chain records Pacific plate motion relative to a long-lived hotspot; the youngest main island is at the southeast end.
Four NOAA surface analysis charts show pressure contours and weather fronts during a North American storm.
NOAA surface analyses during a late-February 2022 storm. Isobars join equal pressure; front symbols identify analysed boundaries between air masses.

CERES measures reflected shortwave energy in W m⁻². Albedo is the fraction of incoming sunlight reflected, so obtaining it requires dividing reflected flux by the corresponding incoming flux; the colour scale here is not albedo.
Tilted and folded sedimentary beds exposed at The Settlands coast.
Folded strata at The Settlands, Wales. Trace a bed through the exposure to see deformation recorded in solid rock.
Satellite image of the parallel folded ridges of the Appalachian Mountains and Chesapeake Bay.
NASA Terra MODIS, 15 September 2023. Appalachian ridges and valleys across Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania preserve the structure of an ancient mountain belt.
USGS map showing the distribution of principal aquifers across the United States.
USGS principal aquifers of the United States, 2000. Colours identify aquifer systems; the map does not show water-table depth or whether a particular well is confined.
Grey London Clay exposed below yellow-brown Red Crag in the sea cliffs at Walton-on-the-Naze, Essex.

London Clay forms the lower part of the Naze cliffs. Clay-rich beds commonly transmit groundwater slowly and can act as aquitards; the cliff exposes the material, while permeability is established by testing.
Glacier ice occupies a steep-sided mountain basin in Denali National Park, Alaska.
Glacial terrain in the Muldrow Glacier area, Denali. Ice erosion enlarges mountain hollows into cirques and sharpens the ridges between them.
Green crystalline mantle peridotite enclosed by darker volcanic host rock at Peridot Mesa, Arizona.

Mantle peridotite enclosed in volcanic host rock at Peridot Mesa, Arizona. It is physical evidence of rock from the upper mantle. The mantle is predominantly solid; local partial melting is not a global magma ocean.
A sequence of dark Venus silhouettes crosses the Sun in SDO ultraviolet observations.

SDO's time sequence of the 2012 Venus transit. Such alignments require the planet to be near an orbital node. Historical transit timing helped determine the Earth–Sun distance, now represented by the precisely defined astronomical unit.
Rounded grey stones and pebbles of different sizes on an English North Sea beach.
Pebbles on the North Sea coast of England. Repeated collisions can round and reduce fragments through attrition; a still image records the resulting grains.

Meteosat-9 observed this day–night boundary on 21 December 2010. Earth's tilted axis puts the subsolar point south of the equator and gives southern latitudes longer days. Declination is the Sun's angle north or south of the equatorial plane; the tilt of the boundary is observational evidence, not an angle scale.
A soil profile on the Karelian Isthmus with a dark surface, pale leached layer and browner subsoil.
Podzolic soil on the Karelian Isthmus. The pale E horizon has lost material by eluviation; material may accumulate in the B horizon below.
Tall orange sand dunes under a clear sky at Sossusvlei, Namibia.
Sossusvlei dunes, Namib Desert. Wind transports loose sand by surface creep and saltation; the dunes record accumulated transport rather than individual grain paths.
Field photographs of red and black soils at different positions on the Addi Selam hillslope in Ethiopia.
Addi Selam, Ethiopia: published field photographs compare red and black soils along a hillslope. Slope position changes drainage and material movement.
Crescent-shaped dunes around Lagoa dos Barros on Brazil's Atlantic coast, seen from the ISS.
Wind shapes barchan dunes beside Lagoa dos Barros, Brazil. The crescent tips point downwind.
Aerial photograph of the Giens peninsula joined to the coast by two narrow sediment barriers.
Giens, near Hyères, France. The double tombolo connects the peninsula to the mainland through two sediment-built barriers.
Landsat view of the thin Chandeleur barrier islands off Louisiana.
Landsat observations of the Chandeleur barrier islands, Louisiana. Narrow sandy islands separate the Gulf of Mexico from shallow coastal waters; storm erosion can fragment and reshape them.
Rounded pillow lava on a fissured seafloor at the Galápagos Rift, photographed by a NOAA expedition.
NOAA, Galápagos Rift, 21 July 2011. Lava quenched in seawater forms pillows close to a spreading centre, where new oceanic crust is built.
A karst spring in Alabama flows over rocks from a wooded limestone slope.
Groundwater emerges at a karst spring in Alabama. Water stored in connected pores and fractures can return to the surface as spring flow.
A mountain basin occupied by glacier ice in the Muldrow Glacier area, Denali. A basin is a low area bounded by higher ground; drainage basins are defined by the area contributing water to an outlet.
A broad, grassy former river valley near Blumberg, now drained by the much smaller Aitrach.

The Aitrach valley preserves the former route of the Feldberg Danube. Capture by the Wutach diverted its large upstream flow towards the Rhine, leaving the small Aitrach in an oversized valley. The channel itself is difficult to distinguish in this landscape view.
Tree roots grow into joints in rock beside a roadside exposure.
Roots grow through existing rock joints. Their growth can widen cracks, contributing to biological and physical weathering.
Grassland with scattered acacia trees in Serengeti National Park, Tanzania.
Serengeti savanna: seasonal rainfall helps explain the balance between grasses and scattered trees.
Angular rock blocks cover the summit of Foel Fras in Wales.
Blockfield on Foel Fras, Wales. Physical weathering breaks bedrock into angular fragments without changing its minerals.
Deep blue Crater Lake fills a broad volcanic depression, with Wizard Island near its western shore.
USGS aerial photograph of Crater Lake, Oregon. Collapse following the eruption of Mount Mazama formed the caldera; Wizard Island is a younger volcanic cone.
Rock contact exposed along the Moine Thrust at Knockan Crag in northwest Scotland.

The Moine Thrust at Knockan Crag juxtaposes rocks with different geological histories. Such field contacts help reconstruct the Caledonian mountain belt and its crustal terranes; boundaries between terranes need regional evidence as well as one outcrop.
Fossilised Ogyopsis klotzi trilobite preserved in dark shale.
Ogyopsis klotzi from the Middle Cambrian Mount Stephen Trilobite Beds, Canada. Fossils help correlate and interpret ancient sedimentary rocks.
Green phytoplankton and sediment-rich water off Mauritania's desert coast, observed by Aqua MODIS.
Aqua MODIS, 5 May 2020. Upwelling in the Canary Current system supplies nutrients off Mauritania. The visible green water contains phytoplankton and sediment; it is not a temperature map.
Green fields and wooded valleys on Exmoor in North Devon.
Exmoor, North Devon: a landscape within the Cfb oceanic climate region. Köppen classes use long-term monthly temperature and precipitation, not the weather on the day of the photograph.
A pale specimen of kaolinite from Ixtassou, France.
Kaolinite from Ixtassou, France, is a clay mineral. Clay as a soil texture means particles smaller than 0.002 mm; mineral identity and particle size are different properties.
Weather instruments inside the enclosure at Charterhall in the Scottish Borders.
Charterhall weather station, Scotland. Standardised instruments measure local conditions; climate describes their statistics over many years.
A low shelf cloud sweeps over buildings at Brock University in Ontario.
A cold front passes Brock University, St. Catharines, Canada. The cloud edge makes uplift visible; the front itself is a zone of contrasting air.
A broad spiral of white clouds over the Pacific northeast of Japan.
MODIS observed this extratropical cyclone northeast of Japan on 22 February 2012. Cloud bands trace the low-pressure circulation.
Floodwater from the Stillaguamish River surrounds a picnic table and trees.

Floodwater on the Stillaguamish River, Washington. Rain-fed regimes respond to precipitation; a flow's competence is the largest sediment it can move, which cannot be inferred from water colour alone.
NASA Blue Marble satellite imagery displayed in the curved-outline Robinson projection.
NASA satellite imagery in Robinson projection. This compromise projection balances several distortions; it preserves neither all areas nor all local angles.

Lava fountains at Kīlauea show magma reaching the surface through a volcanic vent. Its subsurface conduit is inferred from geophysical observations and eruptive behaviour, not visible through the rock.

USGS principal-aquifer map. Aquifers transmit groundwater; low-permeability aquitards can confine them. Confinement and pressure require a geological section and well measurements, and cannot be read from this surface map alone.
The Moselle joins the wider Rhine beside the city of Koblenz, Germany.
The Rhine–Moselle confluence at Koblenz, photographed in 1988. A tributary joins the main channel here.
NASA Blue Marble imagery in Mercator projection, with strongly enlarged high-latitude regions.
NASA Blue Marble imagery reprojected by Mdf into Mercator. Local angles are preserved, area grows towards the poles, and a constant-bearing route plots as a straight line.
A breaking wave curls and foams along the coast at Porto Covo, Portugal.

Wave breaking at Porto Covo, Portugal. Whether waves build or erode this beach depends on the balance of swash, backwash and sediment transport over time; a single breaking crest cannot establish that balance.
Snow-covered Himalayan peaks and valleys photographed from the International Space Station.
The Himalaya from the ISS: crust shortened and thickened as India collided with Eurasia.
NOAA bathymetry map of the South Atlantic showing continental shelves and the mid-ocean ridge.
NOAA South Atlantic bathymetry. Colour represents seafloor depth, revealing continental margins, abyssal basins and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
Open grassland and sparsely vegetated hills near Jargalant, northern Mongolia.
Steppe near Jargalant, Mongolia, far from a moderating ocean. Continental interiors often have larger annual temperature ranges; a weather station's long-term record is needed to measure that range.
USGS topographic map of Mount Rainier with contours, glaciers and named summits.
USGS Mount Rainier topographic sheet, published in 1971. Contours connect equal elevations; close spacing marks steep slopes.
Cyclone Evan's spiral cloud bands cross the islands of Fiji in a NASA satellite image.
Aqua MODIS observed Cyclone Evan near Fiji on 16 December 2012. Its cloud bands spiral around the centre; a mathematical logarithmic spiral is an approximation, not a measured exact fit.
A Deep SOLO profiling float is lowered from the research vessel Kaʻimikai-O-Kanaloa in 2018.

NOAA Deep SOLO deployment, 2018. Profiling floats measure ocean temperature and salinity at depth, helping scientists study density structure and deep circulation. The ocean conveyor is a simplified description of a complex circulation.
Forest canopy at Bodiman, Cameroon. Leaves intercept rain and absorb light for photosynthesis; the photograph shows the living store, not the invisible molecular reactions.
A breaking wave at Porto Covo, Portugal. In shallow water a wave slows and steepens; its crest eventually breaks.
An aerial view of the Oso landslide's bare source scar, debris path and deposits across the valley.
Oso, Washington, 2014: an aerial photograph of the landslide source, travel path and deposit. The displaced material crossed the valley floor.

Mantle peridotite carried to the surface as a xenolith within volcanic rock. It provides a sample of solid upper mantle. The lithosphere includes crust and rigid upper mantle; the green xenolith is not a piece of crust.
Metallic black octahedral magnetite crystals on rock, Smithsonian specimen B10614 from Binnental, Switzerland.

Magnetite, photographed in the Smithsonian collection. Pure magnetite loses its spontaneous magnetic ordering near 580 °C, its Curie temperature. This specimen photograph shows the mineral, not a temperature measurement.
The muddy Ucayali River winds through forest in Peru, with abandoned bends beside the active channel.
Ucayali River, Peru, photographed from the ISS. Meander migration leaves cut-offs and abandoned channels across the floodplain.
Younger gently dipping red sandstone overlies steep grey beds at Siccar Point, Scotland.

The unconformity at Siccar Point records a gap of many millions of years. Ma means million years ago and ka means thousand years ago; those intervals are inferred from geological evidence, not from the photograph alone.
A circular CTD instrument and water-sampling rosette is lowered into the ocean.

NOAA CTD water sampling. Temperature and salinity observations constrain water density and help identify deep-water masses such as North Atlantic Deep Water. The instrument photo does not show the global circulation itself.
False-colour Landsat image of the Lena Delta with many branching distributaries and islands.
Landsat's view of the Lena Delta, 2000. Distributaries spread sediment into the Arctic Ocean. The image combines infrared and red bands.
A streamflow-gauging station beside Huey Creek in Antarctica's rocky McMurdo Dry Valleys.
USGS gauging station at Huey Creek, Antarctica, 12 December 2001. Repeated measurements of stage and discharge produce a river's hydrograph.

GOES-East cloud observations over the Americas, 22 April 2014. Tropical cloud bands and midlatitude systems provide evidence of atmospheric circulation. The three-cell pattern is a long-term zonal average, not three fixed cloud rings in this single image.
Turquoise water fills the steep-sided Bimmah sinkhole in Oman.
Bimmah sinkhole, Oman. Dissolution and collapse in soluble rock can create closed depressions called dolines.
ASTER satellite image of branching tributary valleys near the Colorado River in Canyonlands, Utah.
ASTER, 24 September 2005: tributaries dissect sandstone in Canyonlands, Utah. A drainage network collects flow towards a main river.
Aerial view of elongated low hills around Horicon Marsh, Wisconsin.
Drumlin terrain near Horicon Marsh, Wisconsin. The streamlined hills record former glacier flow; they are landforms left after the ice retreated.
NOAA sea-surface temperature anomaly map with warmer-than-average water across the equatorial Pacific in late 2015.
NOAA, 11 October–7 November 2015: positive sea-surface temperature anomalies extend across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific during El Niño.
USGS topographic map extract showing Yosemite Creek, a campground, contours and coordinate markings.
A real USGS topographic sheet of Yosemite Creek. Read the sheet's coordinate system and scale before giving a position; it is not an OS National Grid map.
The Wutach flows through a narrow, wooded gorge below exposed rock walls in the Black Forest.
Wutach Gorge, Germany. Capture diverted drainage from the Danube system towards the Rhine; subsequent incision cut this gorge.
CERES global map of outgoing longwave radiation with a colour scale in watts per square metre.
NASA CERES, April 2015. Satellite observations map outgoing thermal radiation at the top of the atmosphere in W m⁻²; colder cloud tops generally emit less than warm clear-sky regions.
NASA CERES map of net radiation averaged over 2000–2015, with a −200 to +200 W m⁻² colour scale.

NASA CERES observations, 2000–2015 mean. Net radiation is incoming sunlight minus reflected shortwave and emitted longwave energy at the top of the atmosphere. Positive values indicate a radiative surplus.
USGS scientists install a field seismometer at Sabana Yeguas, Puerto Rico.

USGS seismometer installation in Puerto Rico. Wave arrival times and recorded ground motion are used to estimate an earthquake's focus, epicentre and magnitude; none of those buried locations is visible in this photograph.
NASA Blue Marble satellite imagery displayed in a Mollweide projection with a graticule.
NASA satellite imagery reprojected by Strebe into Mollweide. This equal-area projection preserves relative areas but distorts shapes; the ocean has been lightened for legibility.
NASA Blue Marble satellite composite of Earth in an equirectangular global map.

NASA Blue Marble monthly composite in an equirectangular latitude–longitude grid. Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the equator; parallels run east–west. The geographic reference lines are mathematical, not marks on the land.
Meteosat view of Earth's nearly north–south day–night boundary at the March equinox.
Meteosat-9 SEVIRI, 20 March 2011. The terminator passes close to both poles around the equinox; refraction and the Sun's finite disc mean observed daylight is not exactly twelve hours everywhere.
Landsat view of the Thames estuary, coastal shallows and offshore wind farms.
NASA Landsat observation of the Thames estuary. The tidal river widens towards the North Sea; pale water reveals suspended material and shallow coastal water.
The Aletsch Glacier curves through a steep Alpine valley, with dark medial moraines running along its surface.
The Aletsch Glacier stores water on land. Melting land ice adds water to the ocean and contributes to eustatic sea-level rise; this photograph alone does not quantify a global sea-level change.
Wisps of low fog rise above a calm lake on a frosty morning, with trees reflected in the water.
Evaporation fog over a lake. Water vapour mixes into colder air and condenses into droplets; invisible vapour itself cannot be photographed.
Microscope photograph of leaf epidermal cells and stomatal pores under drought conditions.
Leaf epidermis viewed through a microscope. Stomata regulate gas exchange and water-vapour loss; transpiration is one part of evapotranspiration.
The clear eye and tall spiral cloud walls of Hurricane Isabel, photographed from the ISS.
Astronaut Ed Lu photographed Hurricane Isabel on 13 September 2003. The eye is surrounded by the eyewall's deep convective clouds.

USGS stream-gauging station at Huey Creek, Antarctica. A time series from a gauge reveals a hydrograph's rising limb, peak and falling limb. Lag time compares rainfall timing with the discharge peak; it is not a distance along the river.
Ordnance Survey 1:250,000 map sheet NO of northeast Scotland with the British National Grid.

Ordnance Survey sheet NO, northeast Scotland. British National Grid eastings and northings are measured from a false origin southwest of Great Britain. Four figures identify a 1 km square; six identify a 100 m square. This reduced 1:250,000 sheet illustrates the system; use a detailed map for precise references.
Fallen leaves and organic litter beneath white beech trees in New South Wales, Australia.
White beech leaf litter at Carowiry Creek, New South Wales. Organic material on the forest floor stores carbon and provides material for decomposition.
A line of lava fountains and gas rises from the Kamoamoa fissure in forest southwest of Puʻu ʻŌʻō, Hawaiʻi.
USGS, 5 March 2011: lava erupts along a newly opened fissure between Puʻu ʻŌʻō and Nāpau, Kīlauea. Several fountains mark the linear opening.
The South Fork Stillaguamish River in flood. Water spreads beyond the usual channel when discharge exceeds channel capacity.
NASA CERES observations, 2000–2015 mean. Colours show sunlight reflected by the Earth system in W m⁻². This is outgoing shortwave flux, not incoming solar irradiance or albedo itself.
A rounded specimen of augen gneiss with pale mineral eyes enclosed in dark, folded bands.
Augen gneiss: deformation and metamorphism organise minerals into bands around larger crystals. Rock-cycle pathways need not follow one fixed loop.
A reverse fault offsets contrasting mineral layers in a rock sample from the Stillwater Complex, Montana.
Reverse fault in layered igneous rock from Montana's Stillwater Complex. Trace matching layers across the break: the hanging wall moved up relative to the footwall.
Brown coal exposed at Chukurovo in Bulgaria.
Lignite at Chukurovo, Bulgaria. This fossil fuel formed from buried plant material; combustion transfers its stored carbon to the atmosphere.
An orange windsock extends above a field beside the path to Green Lane Farm.
A field windsock shows near-surface wind direction. Drag from terrain and vegetation slows flow and can turn it across isobars; the pressure gradient itself is not measured by a windsock.
A bank of cloud spills over a mountain ridge above Cilaos on Réunion.
A föhn cloud wall above Cilaos, Réunion. Moist air rises on the windward side; descending air on the lee side warms as it is compressed.
Saturn and its broad rings in a natural-colour mosaic photographed by the Cassini spacecraft.
Cassini, 6 October 2004: a natural-colour mosaic of Saturn and its rings. The rings are a thin disc of orbiting particles.
Swarm-derived maps compare Earth's magnetic field intensity in 2014 and 2025, with a nanoTesla scale.

Swarm satellite observations constrain Earth's magnetic field. Its main source is the moving, conducting liquid outer core, not a permanent bar magnet; the solid inner core and the core's temperature are inferred from other evidence too.
A low grassy coastal terrace below an older cliff near Northbank.

A raised beach at Northbank records former relative sea level. Relative sea level can change through land motion, including glacial rebound, and through eustatic change in global ocean level; the photograph alone cannot separate their contributions.
Photographs of clay samples comparing grey reduced material and oxidised reddish material.
Real clay samples showing contrasting redox conditions. Prolonged saturation restricts oxygen, often producing grey gley colours; oxidation can produce reddish mottles.
A spherical sundial with hour markings and a movable gnomon at Green's Windmill, Nottingham.
A working sundial at Green's Windmill, Nottingham. A gnomon's shadow connects the Sun's apparent direction with local solar time.
Digitised historical sheets of narrow, tapered terrestrial map strips intended to cover a 19-centimetre globe.

Library of Congress: Hondius terrestrial globe gores, reissued by Giuseppe di Rossi in 1615. This is a scan of a real cartographic object; the tapered paper strips were designed to fit a spherical globe. Its historical geography is not a modern reference map.
A groyne extends across the beach at Tallebudgera Creek on Australia's Gold Coast.
Tallebudgera Creek, Gold Coast, in the 1980s. A groyne interrupts sediment movement along a beach and can change sediment supply farther down-drift.
False-colour MODIS brightness-temperature image showing the Gulf Stream and warm eddies in the North Atlantic.
MODIS, 2 May 2001: thermal contrast traces the Gulf Stream and eddies. Brightness temperature includes the sea surface and overlying moist atmosphere.
Bare eroded soil with small gullies on a hillslope near Charters Towers, Queensland.
Hillslope gully and sheet erosion near Charters Towers, Queensland, documented by CSIRO. Loss of cover exposes soil to runoff.
Multibeam sonar bathymetry reveals a broad undersea mountain in the Arctic Ocean.
NOAA multibeam survey of an Arctic seamount. A seamount is a submarine mountain; a guyot is the flat-topped subtype. Surveyed topography, rather than colour alone, is needed to distinguish them.

MODIS observations trace warm Gulf Stream water in the western North Atlantic. The Gulf Stream is one part of the basin-scale subtropical gyre; a single current image does not show the whole circulation.
Crearlagh Burn descends from a higher tributary valley towards a deeper main valley.
The hanging valley of Crearlagh Burn, Scotland. Tributary valleys can be left above a main trough when a larger glacier erodes more deeply.

Meanders on Peru's Ucayali River from the ISS. Bend circulation helps redistribute sediment across the channel. A long profile instead plots bed elevation downstream and requires measured heights; this plan view is not that profile.
Rounded hills and fields around the Vale of Edale, viewed from Grindslow Knoll.
The Vale of Edale and Lose Hill, Peak District, England. A landscape photograph shows local relief, ridges and valley slopes.
Orange and blue atmospheric layers above Earth's curved horizon, with a crescent Moon in the black sky.
Earth's thin atmosphere above the limb, photographed from the ISS on 6 December 2021. Scattered sunlight reveals lower atmospheric layers; coloured bands are not precise altitude boundaries.
The sharp summit and steep ridges of Little Matterhorn in Glacier National Park, Montana.
Little Matterhorn, Glacier National Park, USA. Glacial erosion on several sides can leave a sharp pyramidal peak; this is not the Matterhorn in the Alps.
Voyager 2 image of Neptune's blue disc showing cloud bands and the Great Dark Spot.
NASA/JPL Voyager 2 image assembled from green and orange filter observations in August 1989. Neptune is an ice giant; its displayed deep blue is enhanced relative to its natural appearance.
Ice-wedge polygons in Alaska's Noatak tundra. Repeated thermal contraction cracking and ice growth organise the permafrost landscape.
Sunlight passing through Earth's atmospheric limb in an ISS photograph. At low solar angles, light crosses a longer atmospheric path and spreads across a larger surface area.
An SDO observation of the solar photosphere showing a large dark sunspot group.

NASA SDO observes the solar photosphere and sunspots. The Sun supplies incoming solar radiation (insolation). The solar constant is irradiance near 1 AU on a plane perpendicular to the rays, about 1,361 W m⁻²; it is not measured by this visible-light photograph.
USGS ShakeMap of the 14 August 2021 Haiti earthquake with coloured zones of shaking intensity.

USGS ShakeMap for the 14 August 2021 Haiti earthquake. Intensity varies from place to place and describes shaking effects; magnitude describes the earthquake's overall size. This is the published event-time map, not live hazard information.
Big and Little Diomede islands in the Bering Strait, between snow-covered Russia and Alaska, seen by Landsat 8.

Landsat 8, 6 June 2017: Big Diomede (the larger island, left) belongs to Russia and Little Diomede (right) to the US. The International Date Line passes through the water between them; it is a convention, not a visible physical feature.
An aerial view of damaged buildings and washed-over land on the Bolivar Peninsula after Hurricane Ike.

NOAA photograph of Hurricane Ike damage on the Bolivar Peninsula barrier coast, Texas. Wind stress and low atmospheric pressure contribute to storm surge; the inverse-barometer response is only part of the observed flooding.
Cloud lies below the summit of Cruach Ardrain in Scotland.
Low cloud beneath Cruach Ardrain. A temperature inversion can trap cool, moist air below warmer air; a photograph alone cannot measure the temperature profile.

Cassini's natural-colour mosaic of Saturn and its rings. Orbital period depends on orbital size and the central mass. This image shows one system; it does not preserve the scale of distances across the whole Solar System.
Exposed layers of the Scollard Formation beside the Red Deer River in Alberta.
The K–Pg boundary in the Scollard Formation, Alberta, Canada. The rock record preserves evidence of the transition around 66 million years ago.
Sentinel-6 sea-surface height anomaly map shows lower-than-average levels across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.

Sentinel-6 mapped sea-surface height anomalies during La Niña in January 2025. Ocean–atmosphere coupling changes the Walker circulation and can influence distant weather through teleconnections; these atmospheric links are not directly pictured.
GOES-19 satellite view of a cloud-free band beside western Lake Michigan as a land breeze pushes offshore.

GOES-19, 30 October 2025 at 13:20 UTC. A land breeze keeps clouds away from part of Lake Michigan’s western shore. The product combines visible and infrared observations across the night-to-day transition; station measurements confirm the offshore flow.
Graw DFM radiosondes and a radio receiver arranged on a table.
Balloon-borne radiosondes transmit measurements of the atmosphere. Profiles of temperature, humidity and pressure help locate inversions and estimate lapse rates.
Hawaiian islands with greener windward slopes, drier leeward slopes and silvery sunglint on the Pacific.
Terra MODIS, 27 May 2003. Northeasterly trade winds favour wetter, greener windward slopes; leeward slopes are drier. The bright ocean is sunglint.
A raised embankment separates floodwater from farmland beside the Mississippi at Hannibal, Missouri.
Mississippi levee at Hannibal, Missouri, 20 June 2008. This engineered embankment limits inundation; natural levees instead build up from repeated overbank deposition.
A Hubble mosaic of Andromeda's bright central region, dark dust lanes and densely packed stars.
NASA/ESA Hubble mosaic of Andromeda. Resolved stars and dust lanes provide an observed view of a galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away.

Layered rocks at Grand Canyon record the geological carbon cycle and deep time. Lithification converts sediment into rock; the canyon also exposes much older basement in its inner gorge. A landscape photograph alone does not date individual beds.
National Park Service soil scientists examine a freshly sampled soil profile and record its texture.
NPS fieldwork at Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park. Texture describes the proportions of sand, silt and clay in the mineral soil.
A long-exposure photograph of Orion's stars, red emission nebulae and dark dust clouds.
Orion photographed from ESO's La Silla Observatory by Zdeněk Bardon. Stars that appear close in the sky can lie at very different distances; long exposure reveals faint gas and dust.

The broad, low-gradient lower Ucayali River seen from the ISS. A river long profile follows bed elevation from source to mouth; this photograph shows the lowland reach, while constructing its profile requires elevation measurements.
The Moon appears copper-red during a lunar eclipse viewed from Merritt Island, Florida.
NASA Kennedy Space Center photograph, 20 January 2000. Earth's shadow falls on the Moon; sunlight filtered through Earth's atmosphere gives the eclipsed surface a reddish colour.
EMAG2 global magnetic-anomaly map with alternating anomalies across the ocean floor.

NOAA EMAG2 v3 maps measured magnetic anomalies. Ocean-floor bands record crust formed under changing magnetic polarity. Matching the pattern to dated reversals supports seafloor spreading and allows a rate to be calculated from distance divided by age; colour alone does not give rock age.
NASA ARIA map showing measured ground displacement along the Kamchatka Peninsula after the 2025 earthquake.

NASA ARIA observations of surface displacement following the 2025 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake. The coloured displacement field is measured evidence of movement, not a photograph of the buried fault.
A small stream runs along a valley much larger than its present channel.
A photographed misfit stream. Its present flow is small relative to its valley; former glacial meltwater or a change in drainage may explain the mismatch.
Aletsch Glacier, Switzerland. Flowing ice carries debris; its dark medial moraines record where tributary glaciers join.
A mesquite shrub grows on a mound of trapped sand in the Mojave Desert.
Mesquite in Mojave National Preserve, California. Vegetation traps wind-blown sand and can build a small dune called a nabkha.
First-quarter Moon photographed from Calabria, with the right half of the visible lunar disc sunlit.

The first-quarter Moon is near quadrature. Solar and lunar tidal effects then partly oppose, favouring neap tides; the local minimum tidal range can lag the quarter phase and depends on the coastline and basin.
A thin sunlit lunar crescent with crater shadows along the terminator against black space.
The Artemis II crew photographed this lunar crescent on 7 April 2026. Phase is the visible fraction of the sunlit hemisphere, not Earth's shadow.
Water falls through a narrow rocky step into a dark plunge pool at Cwmorthin, Wales.
Cwmorthin waterfall and plunge pool, Wales. Falling water and entrained sediment erode the pool below the step in the river bed.
Melting snow patches and a stream near Fourth of July Lake in Idaho's Sawtooth Mountains.

Seasonal snowmelt feeds a stream near Fourth of July Lake, Idaho. A nival river regime is strongly influenced by snow accumulation and melt; this photograph shows a snowmelt source, not a measured annual hydrograph.
Blorenge above Llanfoist, with the shallow Cwm Craf hollow visible on its front slope.

Cwm Craf on Blorenge, Wales, has been interpreted as a former nivation hollow. Persistent snow patches can promote weathering and sediment removal without forming a moving glacier. The foreground hollow lies in a glacial moraine.
Afternoon cumulus clouds over Sri Lanka, observed by Aqua MODIS on 9 April 2013.

Aqua MODIS, 9 April 2013. Sea-breeze air moves inland and helps cumulus clouds develop over the warmer island. Silvery water is sunglint. This daytime image shows sea-breeze effects, not a night-time land breeze.
A deep reddish Nipe-series soil profile with a measuring tape in Puerto Rico.
USDA NRCS Nipe-series profile at Cerro Las Mesas, Puerto Rico, January 2002. Classified as Typic Acrudox, this Oxisol formed through deep weathering of iron-rich parent material.
NASA map of low ozone concentrations over Antarctica in September 2023.
NASA Ozone Watch and GEOS-5, 21 September 2023. The mapped ozone hole is a region of depleted stratospheric ozone; colour represents measured or analysed ozone, not a visible opening.
A dark Glossopteris fossil leaf from Permian rocks in Antarctica, with a branching vein network.
Permian Glossopteris leaf from Antarctica. Related fossils on separated southern continents are evidence that these lands were once joined within Gondwana, which formed part of Pangaea.
Hubble observations of Comet ISON's bright coma and tail on 2 November 2013, before perihelion.

Hubble observed Comet ISON on 2 November 2013, before its closest approach to the Sun. Perihelion names that closest orbital point; the coloured filters show coma and tail structure, not a map of the orbit.
NASA SDO observation of active region AR 12192 in 2014. Sunspots are cooler areas of the photosphere; the orange display colour is image processing.
A broad flat river plain with autumn vegetation in the Ahuriri valley, New Zealand.
Ahuriri River plain near Omarama, New Zealand. River deposition builds a relatively flat valley floor between higher ground.
Uneven displaced ground and scarps above the coast at Redcliff Point, Dorset.
Slumping above Redcliff Point, Dorset. Rotational movement displaces blocks along a curved shear surface; the surface scars and tilted ground provide evidence.
Pale pyroclastic deposits fill the Marella River valley below Mount Pinatubo.
USGS photograph of Pinatubo's Marella River valley, 1 July 1991. These are deposits left by pyroclastic flows, not a view of a flow in motion.
A telescopic photograph of the first-quarter Moon on 9 July 2019. Near quadrature, the Sun and Moon lie about 90° apart in our sky.
A thin, dark soil lies directly over jointed granite on Île de Berder, Brittany.
Rankosol over granite on Île de Berder, France. A shallow organic-rich surface over non-calcareous bedrock illustrates a ranker; horizons are real field layers, not a template.
Close-up photograph of a raindrop splashing on soil and throwing droplets and particles outward.
USDA NRCS archive photograph of raindrop impact. Splash detaches and redistributes soil particles before surface runoff carries them farther.
A raised beach near Northbank. Former shorelines record changes in relative sea level, which can include land uplift after unloading of ice.
A rocky opening in grassy limestone terrain at Stream Passage Pot in the Gaping Gill cave system.
Stream Passage Pot, Ingleborough, North Yorkshire. This entrance belongs to the Gaping Gill karst drainage system, where surface water enters underground passages.

SDO recorded Venus crossing the Sun's disc in June 2012. A transit is an observable alignment of orbiting bodies. Revolution means motion around another body; this time sequence is not a scale drawing of the orbits.
South African city lights beneath a curved glowing atmospheric horizon and stars, viewed from the ISS.
South Africa at night, photographed from the ISS. Earth's rotation relative to the Sun defines the solar day; rotation relative to distant stars defines the slightly shorter sidereal day.
Debris, damaged buildings and inundated land at a fishing port near Kesennuma after the 2011 tsunami.

Coastal damage after the 2011 Tōhoku tsunami. Run-up is the maximum vertical elevation reached by the water above a reference sea level; survey evidence is needed to attach a number to this photograph.
Aquarius satellite map of ocean surface salinity with warm colours in saltier subtropical waters.

NASA Aquarius surface-salinity composite, August–September 2011. Colours show salt concentration; black marks missing data. This early product contains calibration artefacts and is not a map of deep-water salinity.
A fishing boat rests on exposed mud beside a wharf at low tide in Nova Scotia.
Low tide at Waterford on St Mary's Bay, Nova Scotia. The exposed harbour floor makes tidal range visible.
Snowmelt near Fourth of July Lake, Idaho. Seasonal melting transfers stored snow water into streams, soils and groundwater.
The dark lunar disc surrounded by the Sun's pale corona during the 2017 total solar eclipse.
NASA's airborne view of the 21 August 2017 total solar eclipse. The Moon blocks the bright photosphere, revealing the corona.

Low water at St Mary's Bay, Nova Scotia. Tidal range changes through the spring–neap cycle as lunar and solar tidal effects combine. This single low-tide photograph does not establish whether it was a spring or neap tide.
The isolated rock stack Hvítserkur rises from shallow coastal water in northwestern Iceland.
Hvítserkur, Iceland. This isolated coastal rock illustrates a stack, with openings cut through its base.
Calcite stalactites hang from the roof of a cave on Mount Kyllini, Greece.
Stalactites in a cave on Mount Kyllini. Dissolved calcium carbonate is deposited as water drips and loses carbon dioxide.
Tropical forest at Bodiman, Cameroon: living vegetation is a carbon store, exchanging carbon with the air and soil.
Bolivar Peninsula, Texas, September 2008. NOAA documented coastal damage from Hurricane Ike's storm surge.
The broad conical slopes of Mount Fuji rise beyond Lake Kawaguchi in Japan.
Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi, Japan. Repeated eruptions built a stratovolcano with layers of lava and fragmental deposits.
The San Andreas Fault cuts through the Carrizo Plain, California. Its surface trace is where the fault intersects the ground; it is only the exposed line of a fault extending through the crust.
The Moon's sunlit crescent photographed from Artemis II. A synodic month is the interval between matching lunar phases, about 29.5 days; one photograph records only one moment in that cycle.
NPS scientists examine soil texture in the field. Sand, silt and clay proportions can be plotted on a ternary texture triangle; the photograph shows the sampled material and fieldwork.
The fully sunlit Earth showing Africa, Arabia, Antarctica and swirling clouds in the Apollo 17 photograph.
Apollo 17's Blue Marble, 7 December 1972. Earth's axial tilt changes the angle and duration of sunlight over the year.
A green auroral band glows below the International Space Station above the southern Indian Ocean.
An ISS photograph of aurora north of Antarctica. Energetic particles excite upper-atmosphere gases; the green light is emitted by the atmosphere, not reflected sunlight.
An exposed bank of poorly sorted glacial sediment containing stones of several sizes.
A natural exposure of glacial till. Ice deposits a mixture of grain sizes directly, often without the sorting produced by flowing water.
South African cities at night from the ISS. Earth's rotation underlies the daily cycle; civil time zones and the International Date Line are agreed conventions, not visible lines on Earth's surface.
NOAA seafloor relief map around Puerto Rico identifies the deep Puerto Rico Trench and nearby plate boundary.

NOAA bathymetric visualisation of the Puerto Rico region. A trench is an elongated seafloor depression associated here with a complex convergent plate boundary; vertical relief is exaggerated in this perspective.

Cassini photographed Saturn and its rings together. Their apparent proportions belong to one perspective view; a true-scale model must use the same length multiplier for every dimension, with foreshortening treated separately.
ECOSTRESS thermal map shows warm urban surfaces in London late at night on 15 July 2022.

ECOSTRESS measured London's land-surface temperatures near midnight on 15 July 2022. Built surfaces remained warmer than many vegetated areas. These are surface temperatures, not standard air-temperature readings.
AMSR-E sea-surface temperature anomalies around northern Australia in the Indo-Pacific warm pool.

AMSR-E, 19 October 2004. This warm-pool region was cooler than its long-term average. Colours show temperature anomalies, not absolute water temperature; a negative anomaly does not mean the water is cold in absolute terms.
A USGS groundwater observation station in Stephen C. Foster State Park, Georgia.
USGS observation well in Stephen C. Foster State Park, Georgia. Instruments record groundwater levels; the water table itself lies beneath the surface.
Rounded remnants of granite emerge from loose weathered material in an exposed rock profile.
Weathered granite documented by GeoDIL. Mineral breakdown and disintegration progressively turn intact rock into weathered material.
Long fault-bounded valleys and escarpments in Kenya's East African Rift, viewed from the ISS.
The East African Rift in Kenya: continental extension is an opening stage of a possible ocean-basin cycle. A rift does not inevitably become an ocean.
Panorama of Bald Eagle Mountain in Pennsylvania with the Route 15 wind gap left of centre and a water gap farther right.

Bald Eagle Mountain, Pennsylvania. The wind gap crossed by Route 15 is left of centre; Hagermans Run occupies a separate water gap to the right. A wind gap lacks the through-flowing river found in a water gap.
Long, wind-eroded rock ridges rise above the desert at Dunhuang, China.
Yardangs at Dunhuang, China. Persistent wind erosion shapes elongated ridges in relatively soft rock or sediment.
The volcanic host of this Peridot Mesa xenolith is described by its source as about 580 ka old: roughly 580,000 years. This dates the host eruption, not the formation of the older mantle fragment.
Earth's atmosphere seen edge-on from the ISS on 6 December 2021. Its coloured bands reveal a thin envelope above the surface.
A mantle xenolith brought to the surface by magma: direct evidence of solid rock within Earth's mantle.
NASA ARIA displacement mapping after the 2025 Kamchatka earthquake. Colours encode surface movement, rather than the colour of the ground.
Siccar Point: Devonian sandstone overlies much older, tilted Silurian beds. The unconformity records deformation, erosion and missing time.
NASA Blue Marble Next Generation, July 2004. A cloud-free satellite composite in a latitude–longitude grid: the map stretches high latitudes and is not equal-area.
South Africa on Earth's night side, seen from the ISS. Rotation carries locations through sunlight and darkness; this is a photograph of the night hemisphere.
An exposed soil profile beneath woodland at Wuhlheide in Berlin, with a measuring tape against the face.
A measured field profile in Wuhlheide, Berlin. Colour and texture vary down the soil; horizon boundaries must be identified from field evidence.
Extreme-ultraviolet observation of the full Sun showing bright active regions, displayed in yellow.
SDO's Atmospheric Imaging Assembly, 18 December 2015. This false-colour ultraviolet observation reveals the hot solar atmosphere, not the Sun's visible colour.
Circular plates of new pancake ice cover the surface of the western Ross Sea in Antarctica.
New sea ice forming in the Ross Sea. Freezing rejects much of the salt into the surrounding water, increasing its density and helping drive polar overturning.
GOES-East, 22 April 2014 at 11:45 UTC. Cloud belts reveal aspects of global circulation; a single image does not outline every atmospheric cell.
Kesennuma, Japan, after the 2011 Tōhoku tsunami. This aerial photograph records inundation damage; it does not show a breaking tsunami wave.
A windsock responds to moving air. Its open mouth faces into the wind; meteorological wind direction names where the air comes from.

Ordnance Survey sheet NO, northeast Scotland. Eastings and northings locate places in the British National Grid. This reduced 1:250,000 sheet illustrates the grid; use a detailed map for precise six-figure references.
MESSENGER global mosaic of Mercury showing its cratered surface.
NASA MESSENGER mosaic of Mercury, 2011. Spacecraft observations reveal the planet's cratered rocky surface; this is a composite, not a single exposure.
USGS seismometer installation at Sabana Yeguas, Puerto Rico, 10 January 2020. Recorded ground motion distinguishes P, S and surface-wave arrivals; the photograph shows the measuring instrument.
NOAA CTD rosette. Conductivity, temperature and pressure measurements describe salinity and density through the water column; bottle samples provide independent checks.

Swarm-based core-field models for 2014 and 2025, in nanoTesla. Satellite measurements constrain the field generated mainly by motion of conducting liquid in the outer core; this is not a photograph of the core.
NOAA Office of Coast Survey multibeam measurements of an Arctic seamount. The coloured relief is a visualisation of measured seabed shape, not an underwater photograph.
NASA SDO, 5–6 June 2012. A time sequence of ultraviolet observations shows Venus crossing the solar disc. The repeated silhouettes are different times, not several planets.

Sentinel-6, 13 January 2025. Lower sea-surface heights accompanied La Niña's cooler equatorial waters. Colours show height anomalies, not sea-surface temperature; seasonal cycles and long-term trends were removed.

NOAA EMAG2 v3 combines satellite, ship and airborne magnetic measurements. Oceanic magnetic stripes record spreading and changing polarity. Colours represent anomalies in nanoTesla, not directly the ages of rocks.
Rocky ridges above Wadi Shahah in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.
Wadi Shahah, UAE. Bare mountain slopes drain into channels that carry water after rain.
Cliffs and cultivated valley floor at Bamiyan, Afghanistan.
Bamiyan Valley, Afghanistan. Steep sedimentary cliffs overlook the cultivated valley floor.
Wooded hills and a road through a valley in Armenia.
Armenia. Wooded slopes and valley routes show how relief shapes access and land use.
Rounded rock outcrops rise above woodland beside the Huambo–Dondo road in Angola.
Angola. Isolated rock outcrops stand above the surrounding wooded landscape.
Clear water in the Río Manso among forested banks in Argentine Patagonia.
Río Manso, Argentine Patagonia. A mountain river flows through a forested valley.
The Salzach valley at Werfen, Austria, seen from Hohenwerfen Castle.
Werfen, Austria. Settlements and transport follow the floor of an Alpine river valley.
Green pasture and scattered trees at Nirimba, Western Australia.
Nirimba, Western Australia. This coastal farming landscape has cool-season rainfall and a dry summer.
Mountain slopes near Lahic in Azerbaijan.
Lahic, Azerbaijan. Steep relief in the Greater Caucasus concentrates movement and settlement in valleys.
Rocky hills and the Trebišnjica valley near Gornji Orahovac, Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Trebišnjica valley, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Rocky relief and confined low ground shape drainage and settlement.
Freÿr limestone cliffs across the Meuse beside the castle gardens in Belgium.
Freÿr, Belgium. The Meuse cuts between wooded slopes and exposed limestone cliffs.
Snow-covered Vihren and Kutelo peaks in Bulgaria's Pirin Mountains.
Pirin Mountains, Bulgaria. Elevation controls snow cover and contrasts with the warmer lowlands.
Pale salt margins around Laguna Honda beneath barren mountain slopes in Bolivia.
Laguna Honda, Bolivia. A high-altitude salt lake occupies a dry Andean basin.
Morning cloud in a valley among forested and cultivated slopes in Bhutan.
Bhutan. Valleys channel drainage through steep Himalayan relief.
Flat green fields and scattered rural buildings in Belarus.
Belarus. Low relief supports broad fields and a dispersed rural landscape.
Green hills above Kamanyola in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Kamanyola, DR Congo. Hills rise beside the Ruzizi Plain within the East African Rift region.
Rock formations and the Tara salt flat in northern Chile's Atacama Desert.
Salar de Tara, Chile. An arid high basin collects salts while exposed rock frames its margins.
The Guáitara canyon and farmed slopes surrounding Las Lajas near Ipiales, Colombia.
Guáitara canyon, Colombia. A deeply incised river separates steep, cultivated slopes.
Rolling green pasture and wooded hills in Costa Rica.
Costa Rica. This hill pasture is one local landscape within a country with strong elevation and rainfall contrasts.
Pedoulas village and wooded slopes in the Troodos Mountains of Cyprus.
Troodos Mountains, Cyprus. Higher ground is cooler and generally wetter than the coastal plains.
Weathered rock towers among woodland in Český ráj, Czechia.
Český ráj, Czechia. Resistant sandstone forms towers above the surrounding forest.
Low, wet grassland and bare trees beneath clouds in Denmark.
Denmark. Low-lying ground and seasonal wetness influence drainage and farming.
Low coastal hills overlooking the sea in Algeria.
Coastal Algeria. Mediterranean hills contrast with the much drier interior of the country.
Cloud and sunlight across wooded mountain slopes in Ecuador.
Ecuador. Mountain relief changes temperature and rainfall over short distances.
Still water and pine trees at Viru Bog in Estonia's Lahemaa National Park.
Viru Bog, Estonia. Waterlogged peatland stores carbon and drains slowly.
Bare, stony plains and rocky mountains in Egypt's Sinai Desert.
Sinai, Egypt. Sparse vegetation exposes an arid landscape shaped by weathering and occasional runoff.
A winter river and snow-covered trees in Finland, photographed in February 1963.
Finland, February 1963. A historical field photograph of seasonal snow beside a river.
Snow-covered Greater Caucasus peaks above the lowland foreground in Georgia.
Greater Caucasus, Georgia. Strong elevation contrasts create different thermal and snow regimes.
Grassy and wooded hills near Boti, Ghana.
Boti, Ghana. Vegetation cover varies across hills and cultivated ground.
Historical photograph of the Roraima escarpment in British Guiana, around 1910–1911.
Roraima region, historical British Guiana. A steep plateau edge rises above the surrounding upland landscape.
Dense urban development around Hong Kong's harbour, seen from the hills in 2005.
Hong Kong, 2005. Steep hills and a deeply indented coast concentrate urban development beside the harbour.
The blue-green Krka River among wooded slopes in Croatia.
Krka River, Croatia. Water flows through a limestone landscape with forested valley sides.
Cultivated mountain slopes at Palmes near Petit-Goâve, Haiti.
Palmes, Haiti. Farming occupies steep slopes where soil cover and runoff management matter.
A broad flowering rapeseed field near Rum, Hungary.
Rum, Hungary. Agricultural fields occupy gently rolling lowland terrain.
Sangeang volcano rises behind coastal islands near Sumbawa, Indonesia.
Sangeang, Indonesia. A volcanic island rises sharply from the surrounding sea.
Rocky coast and low cliffs at Baltimore, Ireland.
Baltimore, Ireland. Atlantic waves act on an exposed rocky shoreline.
Rounded exposed rock and vegetation at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu, India.
Mahabalipuram, India. Weathered crystalline rock is exposed near the Tamil Nadu coast.
Green cultivated ground and tracks near Khabat in northern Iraq.
Khabat, northern Iraq. Cultivated ground contrasts with Iraq's drier central and southern landscapes.
Bare mountain slopes and stony ground near Abyaneh, Iran.
Abyaneh, Iran. Sparse vegetation leaves rock and dry drainage channels exposed.
Harvested fields and scattered trees in Tuscany, Italy.
Tuscany, Italy. Rolling agricultural land reflects a Mediterranean seasonal climate.
Sand and rocky mountains near Wadi Rum in southern Jordan.
Southern Jordan. Sparse vegetation exposes desert rock and sediment to wind and occasional runoff.
Sunset over open grassland and scattered trees in the Maasai Mara, Kenya.
Maasai Mara, Kenya. Seasonal rainfall supports a grassland and woodland mosaic.
Water and tropical trees beside the Angkor Wat complex in Cambodia.
Angkor, Cambodia. Water storage and seasonal rainfall shape the surrounding lowland landscape.
Dark rock walls and trees surround the water at Soesokkak on Jeju, South Korea.
Soesokkak, Jeju. Water drains through the volcanic island's rocky coastal landscape.
Horses in a poppy-covered valley beneath hills near Almaty, Kazakhstan.
Near Almaty, Kazakhstan. Grasslands meet the foothills of the Tian Shan.
A fisherman in a narrow boat among channels of the Mekong at Don Det, Laos.
Don Det, Laos. The Mekong divides around islands in the Si Phan Don river reach.
Historical black-and-white photograph of a hillside town and terraced slopes in Lebanon.
Lebanon, historical photograph. Buildings and cultivated terraces follow the slope of the land.
Clouds and green mountain slopes around Ella Gap in Sri Lanka.
Ella Gap, Sri Lanka. Upland relief channels winds and changes local rainfall.
Historical view from Rambynas Hill across a broad river in Lithuania in the 1930s.
Rambynas Hill, Lithuania, 1930s. The Nemunas valley forms a broad lowland corridor.
Autumn fields, woodland and a rural house in Latgale, Latvia.
Latgale, Latvia. Fields and woodland form a mosaic across gently rolling terrain.
Wind-blown sand and ripples in Libya's desert.
Libya. Wind moves dry sand across dune surfaces.
A sharp dune crest and rippled sand at Erg Chebbi, Morocco.
Erg Chebbi, Morocco. Wind sorts sand and maintains dune crests and slip faces.
Fields, woodland and a village in Hîncești District, Moldova.
Hîncești, Moldova. Settlements and farmland occupy valleys between low wooded hills.
A river cuts through cultivated, reddish slopes in Madagascar.
Madagascar. A river incises cultivated slopes with exposed weathered soil.
Green fields and low hills around Pangetkon in Myanmar's Shan Hills.
Pangetkon, Myanmar. Upland fields and scattered trees occupy the Shan Hills.
Jargalant, Mongolia. A continental interior supports open steppe with strong seasonal temperature contrasts.
Low fields, stone boundaries and buildings on Malta.
Malta. Thin soils and seasonal dryness make soil and water conservation important.
Large cumulus clouds above open fields in Mexico.
Mexico. Cloud development over farmland illustrates the contrast between clear ground and moist rising air.
Forested slopes in the Titiwangsa Range of Pahang, Malaysia.
Titiwangsa Range, Malaysia. Humid tropical conditions support forest on steep mountain slopes.
Isolated rounded rock hills west of Meluco, Mozambique.
Meluco, Mozambique. Resistant inselbergs rise above the lower surrounding terrain.
Stone buildings and terraces in the Sukur cultural landscape, Nigeria.
Sukur, Nigeria. Stone-built settlements and terraces occupy a rocky upland landscape.
Water channels, reeds and snow across flat winter ground in the Netherlands.
The Netherlands. Low relief requires careful drainage and water-level management.
Cultivated slopes, buildings and low clouds at Angare, Nepal.
Angare, Nepal. Steep slopes create short-distance contrasts in access, land use and drainage.
Grass-covered ridges and cloud near Mount Piora in Papua New Guinea.
Mount Piora, Papua New Guinea. High mountain ridges stand above cloud-filled valleys.
Green fields, palm trees and distant hills in central Palawan, Philippines.
Central Palawan, Philippines. Tropical vegetation and farming occupy low ground between hills.
A green mountain valley and bare high slopes in Pakistan.
Pakistan. Elevation creates strong contrasts between cultivated valley floors and exposed mountain slopes.
Fields, scattered trees and low hills in Lesser Poland.
Lesser Poland. Agricultural land occupies gently rolling ground between wooded patches.
Sunset above forested hills at Reserva Mbatoví, Paraguay.
Mbatoví, Paraguay. Woodland covers hills above the surrounding lowlands.
Stony ground and sparse shrubs on Al Aaliya Island, Qatar.
Al Aaliya Island, Qatar. Arid conditions limit vegetation on this low coastal island.
Dry grassland and low rolling hills near Iași, Romania.
Near Iași, Romania. Low hills and open fields form part of the country's eastern agricultural landscape.
Tall weathered rock formations at AlUla, Saudi Arabia.
